When used figuratively or typologically, its broadest conventional association is a complete or divinely appointed season—especially a time of favor, judgment, release, or restoration.","primary_basis":["Isaiah 61:1–2 and Luke 4:18–21 — “the year of the Lord’s favor” denotes the appointed era of salvation proclaimed and inaugurated by Christ.","Leviticus 25:8–13 — the Jubilee year provides the principal biblical pattern for release, restoration, liberty, and return.","Isaiah 34:8 and 63:4 — a “year” can mark an appointed period of divine vengeance or recompense.","Ecclesiastes 3:1 — supports the broader concept of divinely appointed times and seasons, though it does not assign a fixed symbolism to “year.”"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"A literal calendar or regnal year with no symbolic significance. This is the ordinary meaning in most biblical occurrences.","basis":["Genesis 7:11","2 Kings 18:1","Luke 3:1–2"],"prominence":"dominant"},{"meaning":"A Jubilee-like era of salvation, liberation, forgiveness, and restoration.","basis":["Leviticus 25:8–13","Isaiah 61:1–2","Luke 4:18–21"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"An appointed period of divine judgment or recompense.","basis":["Isaiah 34:8","Isaiah 63:4","Jeremiah 11:23"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"In prophetic interpretation, one symbolic day represents one literal year—the “day-year principle.” This is especially prominent in historicist interpretation but is not accepted as a universal rule across Christian traditions.","basis":["Numbers 14:34","Ezekiel 4:5–6","Daniel 9:24–27"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"A standardized 360-day “prophetic year,” commonly inferred by correlating apocalyptic periods such as 1,260 days, 42 months, and “time, times, and half a time.”","basis":["Daniel 7:25","Daniel 12:7","Revelation 11:2–3","Revelation 12:6,14","Revelation 13:5"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"A symbol of completeness simply because a year completes an annual cycle.","basis":["Exodus 23:14–17","Psalm 65:11"],"prominence":"unclear"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"Christian interpretation does not generally treat “year” as carrying one fixed symbolic value. Its meaning is determined by context: most occurrences are literal, while symbolic uses variously concern an appointed season, Jubilee restoration, judgment, or particular prophetic calculations."}
